title: Update on Plan for Live-streaming Parliamentary Sittings
what_it_is: Update on Plan for Live-streaming Parliamentary Sittings

sections.label: Parliament Sitting live-streamed on YouTube
sections.summary: This Sitting is streamed real-time on MCI's YouTube channel, with two live-streams and full video kept six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: As we speak, this Sitting is being streamed real-time on MCI’s YouTube channel, which is accessible to all.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: There will be two live-streams: one with English interpretation of speeches made in vernacular languages, and one without.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: As with current practice, the full video of each live-stream will remain on MCI’s YouTube channel for a period of six months after the end of the Sitting.

sections.label: Public watch proceedings in real time
sections.summary: Live-streaming lets members of the public watch proceedings in real time without being physically present in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: With live-streaming, members of the public will now also be able to watch proceedings in real time, without having to be physically present in Parliament.

sections.label: No sign language, auto-captioning available
sections.summary: There are no provisions for sign language, but the English YouTube stream will have auto-captioning available.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: At this point, we do not have the provisions for sign language.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: However, the English stream on YouTube will have auto-captioning available.
